before.text:
Often the ultraviolet physics is attributed to new degrees of freedom (such as strings).
Could it be that intricate microscopic gauge symmetries and dynamics result in an effective
boundary condition for the low energy description? There is a precedent for such a mechanism
in the Callan-Rubakov effect. A possible relevance to black hole physics was articulated in [8]
and a similar effect could be at play in Euclidean quantum gravity [9]. Lacking an exact
understanding of the microscopic theory, in this article, we will assume as a postulate that
CPT is gauged and analyse its consequences in an example motivated by the study of quantum
black holes.

unit_result_entry.why_material: The source enlarges coordinate inversion into area-preserving transformations of conjugate variables, observes their Hamiltonian action, and shows that at fixed UV they generate an eight-element dihedral action on four phase-space cells. This replaces an inadmissible point identification with a finite canonical symmetry structure.

elements of D4 . A plot of the central causal diamond and the four cells is provided in fig. 1.

4        Conclusions
Inspired by the expectation that there are no global symmetries in quantum gravity, we observe
that treating CPT as a local gauge symmetry leads to an effective boundary condition, relating
points across the two sides of the Penrose diagram that belong to the elementary Planckian

section_entries.mathematical_role: Checks a contrasting observable and finds its continuous spectrum invariant under the proposed identification.

unit_result_entry.title: The same identification leaves light-cone momentum spectra continuous
unit_result_entry.why_material: Applying the boundary map to Kruskal momentum eigenfunctions constrains coefficients but does not discretize momentum. This is a valuable counterpoint: the boundary condition is observable-selective rather than a universal discretizer, and the source reads that invariance as evidence for horizon smoothness.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The smooth-horizon statement is explicitly only a first indication. The exact coefficient relation is less secure than the prose conclusion because of extraction damage.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Uses plane-wave eigenfunctions and a fragmented T2+ coefficient relation. Exact phases and arguments require PDF checking; the conclusion that continuity is unaffected is prose-grounded.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Trivial zeros are mapped to imaginary-energy resonances
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source distinguishes nontrivial real-energy spectral conditions from trivial zeros and interprets the latter through poles and zeros of the scattering matrix on imaginary energy axes as unstable resonances.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The same zero relations may encode missing spectral lines rather than emitted levels
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The conclusion records a materially different Connes-style interpretation: equations (16)-(17) could describe absorption gaps in a continuum rather than a discrete emission spectrum, and deciding among absorption, emission, or both requires comparison of trace formulas with zeta density of states.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Equivalent Hamiltonian normalizations can preserve the scattering matrix while the added boundary condition affects observables selectively: dilation energy becomes discrete in the proposal, whereas light-cone momentum remains continuous.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The equivalences and observable behavior are established only for the cited near-horizon construction, not as a general principle for arbitrary Hamiltonians or boundaries.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Entropy, multiparticle observables, and the missing ground state remain open tests
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source identifies concrete ways the proposal could fail or be sharpened: a density/partition-function calculation must test black-hole entropy and state completeness, multiparticle observables remain unchecked, and the discrete spectrum is still unbounded below despite gauging CPT.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The source offers a layered dictionary—nontrivial zeros as real-energy levels, trivial zeros as imaginary-energy resonances, and possibly zeros as missing continuum lines—while naming density, entropy, multiparticle, and ground-state tests that could distinguish or invalidate these readings.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: These are competing physical interpretations, not mutually verified consequences, and the proposed discriminating calculations are not carried out here.
